title: Platform Fee of the Closing Month — Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service Billing Desk Tool Reference
content:
## The closing-month platform fee

This rule settles the platform fee for the month in which a Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service closes, a month that no later fee debit day can reach because the service is closed by then. For the month in which a service closes, and only for that month, the platform fee is debited on the day the closure is taken and is worked out under this rule; the platform fee of every billing month that ended before the closing month is not set here, and is debited on the tier's fee debit business day of the following month under the rule for completed billing months.

It applies to every tier of the service.

## Booking the fee

The fee is booked with `book_closing_month_fee_4be79540`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

**Capability.** It debits the platform fee for the current calendar month from an employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service as the fee of the month in which the service is closing. One call books one platform fee entry for the current month on the service's ledger, pointing to no other entry, and lowers the service's prefund balance by the amount; the employer sees the fee on its ledger at once. An amount that is not greater than zero, or a fee kind or source other than those described below, books nothing and is reported back.

### Parameters

- `disburse_service_id` — the reference number of the employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service, read from the service record returned by the service lookup (identifier).
- `fee_type` — exactly `monthly_platform`: the platform fee of the month in which the service is closing, the only kind of fee this tool books.
- `related_entry_id` — the reference number of the ledger entry the fee arises from; a closing-month platform fee arises from no ledger entry, so it is passed as an empty string.
- `amount` — the platform fee to debit for the current month, in US dollars as a positive number with exactly 2 decimal places; a value with more decimals is rounded half up to the cent before booking.

### Return

- A one-line confirmation naming the new ledger entry reference (text), the service reference (text), the billing month (YYYY-MM, the current month), the amount debited (US dollars, two decimals) and the prefund balance after the debit (US dollars, two decimals). The entry reference being present means the fee was booked.
- A message beginning "Not booked" means the amount, fee kind or source was not accepted and nothing changed.

### Contract illustration (hypothetical values)

A call with `fee_type` `monthly_platform`, an empty `related_entry_id` and an `amount` of 17.305 books 17.31 for the current month. The same call with an `amount` of 0 returns a message beginning "Not booked", as does a call naming any other fee kind or a source entry.
